headline: Compact support is removable under all positive exponential weights being tempered; positivity on only a finite Laplace domain is insufficient.

theorem.ambient: Finite-dimensional real translation space R^m; arbitrary real Banach value space E; proper closed convex cone C with nonempty interior; T(1)=e in int C.
theorem.replacement_hypothesis: For every integer k>=1 there are finite A_k>0 and N_k>=0 such that ||T(h)|| <= A_k max_{|alpha|<=N_k} sup_y exp(-k|y|)|d^alpha h(y)| for compactly supported smooth h.
theorem.equivalent_replacement_hypothesis: For every a>0, exp(a sqrt(1+|y|^2)) T is a tempered E-valued distribution.
equivalence: The genuine real Laplace transform is in int C at every real g.
Some scalar probability measure with all exponential moments makes T*nu a C-positive distribution.
Some scalar strictly positive smooth probability density p with all exponentially weighted derivative integrals finite makes T*p pointwise C-positive.
theorem.strengthened_output: For every 0<epsilon<1, p can be radial and strictly log-concave, with (1-epsilon)p L_T(grad V) <=_C T*p <=_C (1+epsilon)p L_T(grad V), p=exp(-V)/Z. Output is pointwise interior, has Bochner integral e, and all exponentially weighted derivative norm integrals are finite.
theorem.measure_scope: Includes every finite real signed measure whose bilateral Laplace integrals are finite at every real g in the ordinary Lebesgue sense; no eventual nonnegative tail hypothesis.
theorem.new_proof_step: Global polynomial bounds for translated Bregman-remainder jets, combined with F>=0, control the exponential remainder on all y. A slow radial slope then absorbs weighted seminorm growth and arbitrarily small compact-ball positivity margins.

facts: Total mass one and all exponential variation moments.
A negative atom at every positive integer.
Laplace transform is 1+2 sum exp(-n^2+gn)(cosh(g/4)-1), hence at least one for every real g.
Truncation at every positive integer has a negative rightmost atom, hence eventually negative Laplace transform.

boundary_counterexample.input: For a>0 and 0<c<6/pi^2, let eta=c sum_{n>=1} exp(-a n)n^-2 delta_n, B=eta(R), tau=(1+B)delta_0-eta.
boundary_counterexample.laplace_domain: (-infinity,a], with strictly positive transform throughout that entire maximal finite domain.
boundary_counterexample.obstruction: If tau*nu>=0, then (1+B)nu>=eta*nu. Integrating exp(gx) for any g>a contradicts finiteness of the moment of nu, by Tonelli.
boundary_counterexample.conclusion: No all-exponential probability regularizer exists, even without smoothness, radiality, or log-concavity.
boundary_counterexample.scope_guard: This does not contradict the full-real-domain theorem because tau has no finite Laplace integral for g>a.

charged_inputs: Certified weighted seminorm bounds (A_k,N_k) at every integer exponential rate.
Certified positive lower margins on every finite real g-ball.
Threshold evaluation, normalization, noise preparation, tail control, and any numerical approximation remain separate costs.

audit.convolution_without_compact_support: Proved using the canonical weighted-seminorm extension.
audit.necessity_norm_cutoff_limit: Proved in weighted seminorm before applying T.
audit.normalization_and_moment_interchange: Proved via a Bochner integral in a weighted C^N completion.
audit.large_translation_error: Bounded globally with polynomial factors absorbed by one extra exponential rate.
audit.variable_distribution_orders: Allowed; all order-dependent constants enter G before threshold selection.

literature.katkova_vishnyakova_2001: Primary full text checked. Theorem 1 already covers certain noncompact half-line densities with nonnegative eventual tails; noncompact support itself is not novel.
